name: Baggage Claims MK1, 2 x AA design (Rev B): envelope for the enclosure
status: Nothing here is measured. basis: 'page' = read on a maker's or reseller's page on 22 Nov 2026; 'doc' = the owner's Rev A documents; 'typical' = a common size, unverified; 'calc' = calculated; 'est' = estimate.
supersedes: The packing Rev C was drawn around (3 x AA holder 48 x 58 x 17, perfboard 50 x 70, speaker 5 mm deep, DFPlayer). The owner's ruling of 22 Nov is two AA cells; the speaker that gives the loudness in the design note is 20 mm deep.

frame.z: depth, 42, front face (speaker grille) at z = 0

parts.name: 2 x AA holder, cells in series, with leads
parts.notes: Measure the holder bought before fixing its pocket. Alternative: printed bays with spring contacts.
parts.retention: Ribs at both ends of each cell so a 40 g shock (0.9 kgf per cell, calc) is taken by plastic, not by the contact springs. The lid opens onto the cells.

parts.name: Speaker, 40 mm, 4 ohm, 3 W, paper cone
parts.basis: page (a reseller's page for a 40 mm 4 ohm speaker)
parts.mounting: Rim clamped against the front skin on a 1 mm foam or TPU gasket ring, 36 inside diameter. The front of the cone must be sealed from the back. Not hot glue alone.

parts.name: Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32S3
parts.basis: outline 21 x 17.5 page; height and pads typical

connector.note: 12 clear beyond the socket for a plug; reachable with the lid open. Used only with the battery switch off.

parts.name: Adafruit MPU-6050 breakout, product 3886

mountingHoles.spacingBasis: typical of this board family; UNVERIFIED, check the maker's drawing before printing posts

parts.mounting: Four posts, 5.0 across, 1.8 pilot for M2 self-tapping screws, 5 deep, tops level within 0.1. Rigid: no foam, no tape, nothing else touching the board. On the shell half that carries the loop. Not on the skin the speaker is clamped to.
parts.orientation: Detection does not depend on orientation, except 'inverted': mount with the long edge across the tag (along x) and record which sensor axis faces the loop; the firmware's upX, upY, upZ are set to match (default +Y). The board's printed axis arrows were not read.

parts.name: 3.3 V step-up regulator module (Pololu U1V11F3 class)
parts.keepOut: inductor 5 or more from the speaker magnet (est)

parts.name: Carrier strip of perfboard (optional)
parts.notes: Boards are soldered to it, not socketed. Point-to-point wiring is possible if each board has a pocket.

parts.name: Slide switch, 1 A at 6 V DC or better
parts.basis: typical: choose the 1 A part first, then draw the slot
parts.position: A side wall. Slider recessed 1.0 below the outer surface so a knock cannot move it. Mark OFF and ON.

parts.name: Tactile button, 6 mm
parts.position: Behind a printed flexure tongue on a side wall, 0.2 gap at rest.

packing.note: One packing that closes on paper. Arithmetic only, not modelled.

depthStack.what: front layer: speaker at the top (centre 22 below the top inside edge); below it in 56 x 34: tracker, regulator, MOSFET, capacitor
back layer: holder upright (32 x 58) to one side; beside it a strip 23 x 76 for U1, U2, U3 end to end (66.4 long), switch and button on the side wall
back skin with the card window

speakerCavity.suggested: 3.0 holes (model 3.2) at 6.0 x 5.2 staggered pitch over a 36 round field: 32 holes, 2.3 cm2 (calc). A 30 field (1.6 cm2) is too small.
speakerCavity.gasket: 1 mm closed-cell foam or TPU ring, 36 inside diameter, squeezed 0.3 to 0.5
speakerCavity.mesh: hydrophobic acoustic mesh behind the grille (doc), about 1 dB (est)
speakerCavity.targetLevel: about 80 dB at 1 m at 1 W (calc from a data-sheet sensitivity of 80.5 dB at 1 W and 1 m)

tolerancesPETG.process: 0.4 nozzle, 0.2 layers (doc). Per side unless said. Confirm with a coupon on the printer and spool used.

snapLatch.formula: strain = 1.5 x thickness x deflection / length^2

walls.reason: Target: tag on a case dropped 1.0 m onto concrete, six faces (est). 2.0 is five solid perimeters with no infill line to split along. Ribs under the cells and beside the speaker magnet; neither may load the latch. A screw as well as the latch. Layers not across the loop's pull or the latch's bend.
